# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_019_page_001.jpg

---

**1** But upon the ungodly, wrath fell without mercy and without end — because God already knew what they would do:

**2** they would themselves permit the Israelites to leave, would even press them to go with urgency — and then they would change their minds and come after them.

**3** They were still at the gravesides, still deep in mourning for their dead, when they reached a fresh foolish decision and went off in pursuit of the people they had just expelled with urgent pleas.

**4** But the fate that was rightfully theirs was pulling them toward exactly this end. It made them forget everything that had already happened, so that what was still lacking in their punishment could now be filled.

**5** Your people would pass through the sea by a way that defied all reason. The Egyptians would die a death utterly unlike anything before.

**6** For the whole of creation was being remade in its natural order, freshly rearranged, obedient to your specific commands — all so that your children would come through without harm.

**7** There it was — the cloud hanging over the camp, and dry land rising where water had been. Out of the Red Sea, an open road. Out of the raging flood, a level grassy plain.

**8** And through it the whole nation marched, guarded by your hand, watching wonder after wonder unfold before their eyes.

**9** They frolicked like horses turned out to pasture. They leaped like lambs at play. They praised you, Lord, you who had set them free.

**10** They remembered, even then, what it had been like in Egypt: how the land had brought forth swarms of gnats instead of livestock, and frogs teeming from the river instead of fish.

**11** And then, afterward, they witnessed something new entirely — a fresh kind of bird — when their hunger drove them and they clamoured for better food.

**12** Quails came rising up from the sea, and that was their answer.

**13** But punishment fell on the sinners — not without fair warning. The thunder had already announced it. They suffered according to their own wickedness, and justly so, for they had shown a more savage hatred toward outsiders than anyone before them.

**14** The Sodomites had merely refused entry to strangers they did not know. But these Egyptians had enslaved guests who had done nothing but bless them.

**15** There will be a separate accounting for those earlier sinners, since at least they greeted strangers with hostility from the start. The Egyptians celebrated the Israelites' arrival —

**16** welcomed them with festivals, gave them the same rights as citizens — and then broke every bond of hospitality and crushed them with brutal forced labour.

**17** So they were struck blind: just like the men gathered around the door of Lot, the righteous man — each one groping through impenetrable darkness for his own front doorway.

**18** For the elements of creation changed places with each other. Think of a harp: the strings are the same, the rhythm stays the same — but rearranged, they produce a completely different melody. That is what you can observe happening here, if you look carefully enough.

**19** Creatures of land became creatures of sea. Things that swam transferred themselves onto dry ground.

**20** Fire held its power inside water. Water forgot that its nature is to extinguish.

**21** Flames did not sear the flesh of the perishable creatures wandering through them. And those flames did not dissolve the ice-like crystals of manna — heavenly food that could have melted in a moment.

**22** In all things, Lord — in every single thing — you exalted your people and wrapped them in glory. You were present with them, at every time, in every place.
